newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gene-food law should include seeds - German farmers.
newsitem.headline: Gene-food law should include seeds - German farmers.

text.p: European Union laws on the labelling of genetically modified foods should be extended to seeds, German farm union DBV said in a statement.
The regulation, which comes into effect today and is referred to as the novel-food law, defines market authorisation procedures for food and food ingredients.
DBV said the law would help inform consumers and re-establish their trust in food companies.
It would make genetically engineered food products identifiable and ensure that only foods bearing no risk for the consumer's health were approved.
But DBV president Gerd Sonnleitner said farmers should be given similar choices -- they should be able to decide whether or not to buy seeds derived from genetically modified organisms.
The novel food law is a highly political issue in the wake of the mad-cow beef scare and rows about EU authorisation for market release of gene-altered maize and soybeans.
